concepts.why: The answer only declares an int loop counter. It says nothing about int's range or how int arithmetic works.

Using <= data2.length treats data2.length as the last valid index (the everyday counting reading). The last index is actually data2.length-1, so data2[data2.length] throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

concepts.quote: for (int i = 0; i <= data2.length; i++) copy[i] = data2[i];
concepts.why: The header and body are set up correctly to step through the indexes, but the bound runs one pass too far.
It copies the elements one by one into copy, but it never creates the new array (new int[data2.length]), and the off-by-one bound makes it crash.
